searchText: In my experience the opposite is true. Having http and ws on different parts causes problems and doesn't help anything. Every websocket library I know of can negotiate http to ws upgrade because that is a very integral part of the protocol. It has always annoyed me greatly that geth split http and ws across two different ports, and from a dapp developer perspective it just causes discomfort. The new port for Engine API is to separate inter client communication channel from JSON RPC API. And we should enforce authentication on this channel. I think `8545` should stay as is, `8550` that exposes `engine_` and a subset of `eth_` required by CL should have authentication. QQ: should we also add authentication to `eth_` on port 8550? I thought about adding auth on module level (`engine_`) or method level. I still argue that `eth_` namespace should not be fully exposed on the engine API channel. The *entire* Engine API channel should be authenticated. My general assumption here is that it is probably easier to do authentication on the entire channel rather than individual methods. Is this not the case for Nethermind? I think there is no big implementation difference. I would be in favour of enforcing auth for entire endpoint. Is there any complexity with that? In order to properly specify a subset of `eth_` methods in the Engine API I encourage every client team to fill out the table in this document. https://hackmd.io/E9VKRcmRSc2Imo8RBtqxlw cc <@&595681771690000403> <@&595683609080365088> <@&595683849225240704> <@&595681804422479873> <@&836981489430036500> sending !vibes for the merge 🐼
